chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Mansur al-Sayqal and al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays — both said:
We heard Abu Abdillah (AS) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (SAWW) said: "Allah Mighty and Majestic Said:'

'I do not Hesitate with regards to anything I Do like I Hesitate regarding the death of My Momin servant. I Love to Meet him and he dislikes death, so I Defer it from him; and he supplicates to Me, so I Answer him, and he asks Me, so I Give him; and if there did not happen to be in the world except for one Momin from My servants, I would Suffice with him from the entirety of My creatures, and I would Make his Iman a comfort for him, so that he would not feel estranged toward anyone.'

key_terms.أُنْسًا: comfort/intimacy — the spiritual companionship and sense of peace that Allah instills in the Momin directly from their own iman
key_terms.تَرَدَّدْتُ: I hesitated/wavered — a divine expression denoting the utmost solicitude Allah bears for the death of His believing servant, not implying doubt but supreme care
key_terms.عَبْدِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِ: My Momin servant — the believing slave whose faith establishes a unique and cherished bond with Allah
key_terms.فَأَصْرِفُهُ: so I defer/avert it — Allah's act of postponing death out of regard for the servant's aversion to it, demonstrating divine mercy
key_terms.لَاسْتَغْنَيْتُ: I would suffice/be content — Allah's declaration of self-sufficiency through even a single true believer, affirming the immense worth of iman in His sight
key_terms.لِقَاءَهُ: his meeting — the encounter of the Momin servant with Allah, which Allah loves and which constitutes the spiritual reality of death for the believer
key_terms.يَسْتَوْحِشُ: feels estranged/lonely — to experience desolation or a yearning need for other than Allah, which the Momin's iman-derived intimacy entirely negates

ai.seo_question: What does Allah say in hadith qudsi about His love for the believing servant and their death?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet (SAWW), articulates Allah's singular regard for the Momin servant: His 'hesitation' over their death — born of His love for their encounter with Him — His unfailing response to their supplications, and His declaration that one true believer would suffice Him from all creation. It culminates in Allah's promise to bestow upon the Momin such intimacy from their own iman that they experience no loneliness or yearning toward any other being.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Mansour Al Sayqal and Al Moalla Bin Khunays who both said,
‘We both heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said:

‘Iazwj do not Hesitate with regards to anything Iazwj Do like Iazwj Hesitate regarding the death of Myazwj Momin servant. Iazwj Love to Meet him and he dislikes the death, so Iazwj Exchange it from him; and he supplicates to Meazwj, so Iazwj Answer him, and he asks Meazwj, so Iazwj Give him; and if there did not happen to be in the world except for one Momin from Myazwj servants, Iazwj would have Sufficed with him from the entirety of Myazwj creatures, and would have Made his Emān to be a comfort for him, (so that) he would not yearn to anyone’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Mansur al-Sayqal and al-Mu’alla ibn Khanis who have said the following:
“We heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘

I never hesitated in doing anything as I do about the death of My believing servant. I love to meet him but he dislikes death and 1 then hold it back from him. He prays to Me and I answer his prayers, he asks Me for help and I provide him help. Had there been even only one of my believing servants he would have been sufficient for Me of all others and I would make his belief to provide him company so that he would not feel frightened from anyone.’”
